Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple Scab
Apple___Apple_scab.description: Apple scab is a disease of apple trees caused by the ascomycete fungus Venturia inaequalis. It manifests as dull black or grey-brown lesions on the surface of tree leaves, buds or fruits.
Apple___Apple_scab.remedy: Remove fallen leaves and fruit to reduce the spread. Apply appropriate fungicides like Captan or Myclobutanil during early spring. Ensure proper pruning for air circulation.

Apple___Black_rot.name: Apple Black Rot
Apple___Black_rot.description: Black rot is a disease caused by the fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa, which can infect the fruit, leaves, and bark of apple trees.
Apple___Black_rot.remedy: Prune out dead or diseased wood. Remove all mummified fruit from the tree. Use copper-based fungicides early in the season.

Apple___healthy.name: Healthy Apple Leaf
Apple___healthy.description: The leaf shows no signs of fungal, bacterial, or viral diseases.
Apple___healthy.remedy: Maintain good agricultural practices, ensure proper watering, and fertilize as needed.

Potato___Early_blight.name: Potato Early Blight
Potato___Early_blight.description: Early blight is a common tomato and potato disease caused by the fungus Alternaria solani. It produces target-like spots on older leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.remedy: Practice crop rotation. Ensure plants are properly spaced. Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or copper.

Potato___Late_blight.name: Potato Late Blight
Potato___Late_blight.description: Late blight is a potentially devastating disease caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans. It causes rapid browning and wilting of leaves.
Potato___Late_blight.remedy: Destroy infected plants immediately. Avoid overhead watering. Use resistant varieties and apply fungicides preventatively.

Potato___healthy.name: Healthy Potato Leaf
Potato___healthy.description: The leaf is healthy and shows no signs of disease.
Potato___healthy.remedy: Continue standard care, including regular watering, fertilizing, and monitoring for pests.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Tomato Bacterial Spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot is caused by Xanthomonas species. It causes small, water-soaked, dark spots on leaves and fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.remedy: Avoid overhead watering. Apply copper-based bactericides. Remove and destroy infected plant debris.

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Tomato Early Blight
Tomato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease causing 'bullseye' spots on lower leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.remedy: Remove infected lower leaves. Water at the base of the plant. Use a fungicide containing chlorothalonil.

Tomato___healthy.name: Healthy Tomato Leaf
Tomato___healthy.description: The leaf is vibrant, green, and healthy.
Tomato___healthy.remedy: Maintain optimal watering, apply balanced fertilizer, and ensure good air circulation.
